name: sen_sero_naming_priority
description: Which serovar name to report when an antigenic formula names several. This is a NOMENCLATURE decision, not an antigen test: the pairs below are indistinguishable by wzx/wzy and, for Brikama/Goldcoast, indistinguishable by slide agglutination in a reference laboratory (PMC9150820). The block makes the convention explicit and auditable instead of leaving it to the order rows happen to sit in.
license: gspec curation (nomenclature convention), not upstream data

rules.note: C2-C3:r:l,w — the H1 spellings r and r,[i] are one antigen, and the two rows they key (Goldcoast, Brikama) are the same formula. Evidence: a reference laboratory's agglutination result was literally 'Goldcoast or Brikama' (PMC9150820, SAMN26764377 / SAMN26764405); PMC8552638 submitted its isolate A030_06/19 as Goldcoast with the same in-silico ambiguity; SISTR reports Goldcoast. Brikama has no public genome at all, so no sequence evidence can ever prefer it.

C2-C3:r:1,5 — same r/[i] spelling pair. Bovismorbificans is O:6,8,20 and Hindmarsh is O:8,20, but the O:6 factor has no marker in the rfb cluster (13 complete genomes, 3220 CDS clusters, no cluster splits the groups). Evidence: SISTR reports Bovismorbificans; SeqSero2's curated rename_dict maps Hindmarsh to Bovismorbificans (the WHO merge).

6,8,20:e,h:1,2 — a single formula key that literally carries two serovar names. Newport is the common serovar; SeqSero2's rename_dict maps Bardo to Newport and comments that Bardo is exceedingly rare.
